newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA COURT RULES NEWCREST LEASES VALID.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA COURT RULES NEWCREST LEASES VALID.

text.p: Australia's High Court on Thursday ruled that leases held by Newcrest Ltd to mine within Kakadu National Park in the country's north were valid.
The ruling overturned an earlier court decision.
Newcrest said on Thursday it was still examining the ruling.
The leases cover prospective gold fields and are jointly held by Newcrest, North Ltd and Plutonic Resources Ltd. Newcrest manages the joint venture.
"It's much too premature," Newcrest spokesman David Sassoon told Reuters. "We're still poring over a 100-page document."

Kakadu National Park is a vast conservation reserve which boasts one of the country's most spectacular wetlands, but also rich deposits gold. It has been a controversial battle ground for miners and environmentalists over the years.

The former Labor government ruled in the late 1980s against mining in all but a fraction of the 19,500 sq km (12,200 sq miles) park. One explored area of the park, Coronation Hill, holds proven reserves of 650,000 ounces of gold, 100,000 ounces of palladium and 30,000 ounces of platinum.
